html:
The Book of Kells is an illuminated manuscript of the four Gospels in Latin, made about 800 by Irish monks. It is the greatest work of early Irish art.

It was probably begun at the monastery on Iona in Scotland, founded by the Irish saint Columba, and finished at Kells in Ireland after the monks fled Viking raids. Its pages are covered in knots, spirals, animals and human figures in rich colours, so intricate that some details can only be seen with a lens.

It shows the high culture of Irish monasteries, which kept Latin learning alive and sent missionaries to Britain and the continent, a tradition begun by Saint Patrick. The book has been in Trinity College Dublin since the 1600s, where it is one of the most visited sights in Ireland. Compare the Abbey of Saint Gall.
sum: The Book of Kells is an illuminated manuscript of the four Gospels in Latin, made about 800 by Irish monks. It is the greatest work of early Irish art.
